an5.54:1.1: “Bhikkhus, there are these five unfavorable occasions for striving.
an5.54:1.3: (1) “Here, a bhikkhu is old, overcome by old age.
an5.54:1.4: This is the first unfavorable occasion for striving.
an5.54:2.1: (2) “Again, a bhikkhu is ill, overcome by illness.
an5.54:2.2: This is the second unfavorable occasion for striving.
an5.54:3.1: (3) “Again, there is a famine, a poor harvest, a time when almsfood is difficult to obtain and it is not easy to subsist by means of gleaning.
an5.54:3.2: This is the third unfavorable occasion for striving.
an5.54:4.1: (4) “Again, there is peril, turbulence in the wilderness, and the people of the countryside, mounted on their vehicles, flee on all sides.
an5.54:4.2: This is the fourth unfavorable occasion for striving.
an5.54:5.1: (5) “Again, there is a schism in the Saṅgha,
an5.54:5.2: and when there is a schism in the Saṅgha there are mutual insults, mutual reviling, mutual disparagement, and mutual rejection.
an5.54:5.3: Then those without confidence do not gain confidence, while some of those with confidence change their minds.
an5.54:5.4: This is the fifth unfavorable occasion for striving.
an5.54:5.5: “These are the five unfavorable occasions for striving.
an5.54:6.1: “There are, bhikkhus, these five favorable occasions for striving.
an5.54:6.3: (1) “Here, a bhikkhu is young, a black-haired young man endowed with the blessing of youth, in the prime of life.
an5.54:6.4: This is the first favorable occasion for striving.
an5.54:7.1: (2) “Again, a bhikkhu is seldom ill or afflicted, possessing an even digestion that is neither too cool nor too hot but moderate and suitable for striving.
an5.54:7.2: This is the second favorable occasion for striving.
an5.54:8.1: (3) “Again, food is plentiful; there has been a good harvest and almsfood is abundant, so that one can easily sustain oneself by means of gleaning.
an5.54:8.2: This is the third favorable occasion for striving.
an5.54:9.1: (4) “Again, people are dwelling in concord, harmoniously, without disputes, blending like milk and water, viewing each other with eyes of affection.
an5.54:9.2: This is the fourth favorable occasion for striving.
an5.54:10.1: (5) “Again, the Saṅgha is dwelling at ease—in concord, harmoniously, without disputes, with a single recitation.
an5.54:10.2: When the Saṅgha is in concord, there are no mutual insults, no mutual reviling, no mutual disparagement, and no mutual rejection.
an5.54:10.3: Then those without confidence gain confidence and those with confidence increase in their confidence.
an5.54:10.4: This is the fifth favorable occasion for striving.
an5.54:10.5: “These are the five favorable occasions for striving.”
